mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which can lead to increased borrowing and investment, thereby driving up equity prices and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the federal funds rate increases while equity returns remain positive, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate remains below 5% but the S&P 500 experiences negative returns, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) coupled with a decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a robust labor market, which can drive up aggregate demand and lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If both payroll employment increases and unemployment decreases but the S&P 500 does not experience positive returns, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals increased economic activity, which can lead to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If industrial production increases but the S&P 500 experiences negative returns, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates economic growth, which can lead to higher consumer and business spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If real GDP increases but the S&P 500 does not experience positive returns, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates tighter monetary policy, which can increase borrowing costs and reduce investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the federal funds rate rises above 4% but the S&P 500 experiences positive returns, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% coupled with an increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which can drive up aggregate demand and lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If both the unemployment rate decreases below 5% and payroll employment increases but the S&P 500 does not experience positive returns, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates inflationary pressures, which can lead to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the consumer price index increases above 240 but the S&P 500 experiences positive returns, this hypothesis is rejected.
